name: 2nd Sunday in Lent
description: The struggle of faith and perseverance in prayer.
biblicalBasis: The Canaanite woman who does not give up even when Jesus seems dismissive: 'Lord, help me!... Even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master's table' (Matt 15:21-28). Jacob's wrestling with God at Jabbok: 'I will not let you go unless you bless me' (Gen 32:24-30). Hebrews 11 on the witnesses of faith who held fast.
significance: Faith is not passive feelings but an active struggle — holding on to God even when He seems silent or dismissive. The Canaanite woman's faith is exemplary precisely because she does not give up. Jacob receives a new name (Israel = 'he who struggles with God') — the struggle of faith changes identity.
liturgicalContext: Purple color. In the middle of Lent, the theme of perseverance in faith deepens — preparation for Easter requires steadfastness.
history: This Sunday has traditionally focused on the struggle of prayer. Luther emphasized Anfechtung — the affliction where faith is tested and strengthened through doubt and struggle.
otConnections: Jacob at Jabbok (Gen 32:24-30) is the central Old Testament text. Hannah who prays with tears in Shiloh and does not give up (1 Sam 1:9-20). Moses who holds his arms up in battle against Amalek (Exod 17:8-13) — perseverance in prayer during war.

references.reason: The day is about the struggle of faith and perseverance in prayer. The text about asking, seeking, and knocking, and that God's answer is given, emphasizes that faith is an active struggle where we hold on to God's promise to give good gifts.

The account of the officer's faith (vv. 5-13) is an example of 'faith without seeing' and boundless trust in God's word, which is a central theme for the 2nd Sunday in Lent (the struggle of faith and perseverance).
The call to total dedication and following ('let the dead bury their own dead') emphasizes the requirement for repentance and prioritizing God's kingdom, which is central during Lent.
John the Baptist's death is the main text for the 2nd Sunday in Lent. The text shows the prophet's suffering and prepares for Christ's suffering, which is a main theme for this Sunday in Lent.

The day is defined by the parable of the Canaanite woman (Matt 15:21-28). The text illustrates the struggle of faith and perseverance where the woman does not give up even when Jesus seems dismissive, which is the main theme for the 2nd Sunday in Lent.
